newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila court stops hotel sale to Renong.
newsitem.headline: Manila court stops hotel sale to Renong.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Monday blocked the sale of the historic government-owned Manila Hotel to Malaysia's Renong Berhad.

A Philippine company, which had also bid for the project but lost in the award of the contract in 1995, had filed a petition with the Supreme Court saying the Manila Hotel should not be sold to a foreign company since it was a historical building.
The Supreme Court ordered the Government Service and Insurance System (GSIS), the owners of the hotel, to "accept the matching bid of petitioner Manila Prince Hotel Corporation."
"How much of national pride will vanish if the nation's cultural heritage is entrusted to a foreign entity ?" the decision by the 15-member Supreme Court bench said.

"On the other hand, how much dignity will be preserved and realised if the national patrimony is safekept in the hands of a qualified, zealous and well-meaning Filipino ?", it said, adding: "This is the plain and simple meaning of the Filipino First Policy provision of the Philippine Constitution."

The court ordered the GSIS to accept Manila Prince's bid "to purchase 51 percent of the shares of the Manila Hotel Corporation at 44 pesos per share and thereafter to execute the necessary agreements and documents to effect the sale."
The Manila Hotel, considered one of the great luxury heritage hotels in Asia and facing Manila Bay, was used as U.S. military headquarters during World War II.
But in recent times, the hotel had been losing out to newer hotels in Makati, the country's main financial district.
